etadakkhā.example_2: na cāpi me koci naṃ etadakkhā;

tuṇṇo.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading of nunno in the verse; past participle of √tur 'hurry', used here in the sense 'released (quickly)'. The PEU treats it as an indeclinable 'quickly', but the syntax of the sentence points to a participle agreeing with saro.
tuṇṇo.example_1: Nunno [nuṇṇo (ka. sī. syā.), tuṇṇo (ka.)] saro sarabhaṃ hantu khippaṃ, annañhi etaṃ varapañña rañño.
tuṇṇo.translation_1: Let the released arrow quickly strike the Sarabha deer, for this, O wise one, is food for a king.

paricāriyanto.meaning_2: being attended (by); being served (by); being waited on (by)
paricāriyanto.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Masculine nominative singular agreeing with the addressee (the king); the agent is in the instrumental (nārīgaṇehi). Causative passive sense.
paricāriyanto.example_2: Nārīgaṇehi paricāriyanto, modassu raṭṭhe tidiveva vāsavo.
paricāriyanto.translation_2: Attended by groups of women, rejoice in the kingdom like Vasava in the heaven of the Thirty-three.

ujjhuntu.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Imperative plural of a causative formation, printed as an alternative to oḍḍentu in the text.
ujjhuntu.example_1: 3. Oḍḍentu [ujjhuntu (syā. ka.) aṅguttaranikāye passitabbaṃ] vāḷapāsāni, yathā vajjhetha so dijo;
ujjhuntu.translation_1: “Set a horsehair snare, so that this bird may be captured;

iṇadānaṃ.meaning_2: debt payment; repayment of debt; lending money (at interest)
iṇadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Compound of iṇa (debt) and dāna (giving, payment). Nominative and accusative singular in the verse; it heads a list of livelihoods together with kasivāṇijjā.

hātūna.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Absolutive in -tūna from harati (√har 1), with the root vowel lengthened. In the text it describes carrying food to the young with the beak. The PEU entry hātuna is the same form.
hātūna.example_2: Tesaṃ tuṇḍena hātūna, muñce pubbakataṃ [pubbe kataṃ (sī.)] iṇaṃ.
hātūna.translation_2: Having carried [food] to them with my beak, I release the debt performed previously.”

tavassabyamhi.meaning_2: in the hermitage; in the ascetic's dwelling
tavassabyamhi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading tavassabyamhi (see ka.) has the same meaning. Locative singular in the text; cp. tavassamaṅgaṇa.
tavassabyamhi.example_1: 15. Bhuttañca pītañca tavassamamhi [tavassabyamhi (ka.)], rattiñca [ratī ca (sī. pī.)] no kosiya te sakāse;
tavassabyamhi.translation_1: “Having eaten and drunk in your hermitage, and [enjoyed] the night, Kosiya, in your presence;

santappayi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Aorist or causative form in -i used as a past tense in the verse; dpd peū splits saṃ + tapa + ṇaya + ī. Alternatively an aorist of santappati. Takes an object in the accusative (samaṇabrāhmaṇe).
santappayi.example_2: Annena pānena pasannacitto, santappayi samaṇabrāhmaṇe cāti.
santappayi.translation_2: With a pleased mind, through food and drink, he satisfied ascetics and brahmins, and so on.”

osaṭṭhi.meaning_2: sinking (into); affliction; alternative reading for osīdi
osaṭṭhi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading (ka.) for osīdi in the verse, with osadhi (sī. syā. pī.) and osati (abhinavaṭīkā) as other readings; the meaning is uncertain, so this may be a misreading rather than a distinct word.
osaṭṭhi.example_1: 19. Osīdi [osadhi (sī. syā. pī.), osaṭṭhi (ka.), osati (abhinavaṭīkā), osīdati (?)] me dukkhaṃ [dukkhaṃ me (sī. pī.)] hadayaṃ, me ḍayhate nitammāmi;
osaṭṭhi.translation_1: My suffering has sunk into my heart, it is burning, I am exhausted;

osati.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading of osīdati in the Jātaka verse; ava- > o-. Only the 3rd singular occurs here.
osati.example_1: 19. Osīdi [osadhi (sī. syā. pī.), osaṭṭhi (ka.), osati (abhinavaṭīkā), osīdati (?)] me dukkhaṃ [dukkhaṃ me (sī. pī.)] hadayaṃ, me ḍayhate nitammāmi;
osati.translation_1: My suffering has sunk into my heart, it is burning, I am exhausted;

milayāmi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading of milāyāmi (1st person singular present) in the verse; some editions read miyyāmi. 1sg present in the text.
milayāmi.example_1: 20. Tiṇamiva vanamiva milāyāmi [milayāmi (sī.), miyyāmi (sī. pī. aṭṭha.)], nadī aparipuṇṇāva [aparipuṇṇiyāva (sī. pī.)] sussāmi;
milayāmi.translation_1: I wither like grass, like a tree; I dry up like a river that is not full;

ayyire.meaning_2: venerable sir; reverend sir; noble one
ayyire.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Metathesis of ariya (y and r swapped). Used in address (vocative) in the verse. The manuscript variant ayyire is likely a sandhi or spelling for ayyira before brahme.
ayyire.example_1: 42. Vande te ayirabrahme [ayyire brahme (ka.)], yo me icchitaṃ patiṃ varākiyā;
ayyire.translation_1: I revere you, noble brahmin, who gave me back my beloved husband, a wretched woman's [husband];

makā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading (sī. pī.) for akāsi in these verses; 3rd singular aorist of karoti. In pada 1 the subject is vihaṅgamo, in pada 2 mā ... makāsi is prohibitive.
makā.translation_1: It is too difficult to do, the work the bird did for the egg-born;
makā.example_2: Mā me paripanthamakāsi [makā (sī. pī.)], saggaṃ mama patthayānassa ’’.
makā.translation_2: Do not cause an obstacle for me, aspiring for heaven.”

yañcaretha.meaning_2: that a son should practise (for his father); which a son should perform
yañcaretha.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text yaṃ ... caretha is written yañcaretha. The variant pitu yañcaretha shows the same sandhi. Caretha is optative 2nd plural of carati; the subject putto is construed with the singular sense. Alternative resolution yaṃ + caretha. In yaṃ care the same phrase resolves as yaṃ + care.
yañcaretha.example_1: 53. Addhā hi tāta satamesa dhammo, putto pitu yaṃ care [pitunaṃ care (ka.), pitu yañcaretha (sī. pī.)] atthacariyaṃ;
yañcaretha.translation_1: Yes, dear, this is the Dhamma of the wise, that a son should perform the duty of a father;

suhaddayañca.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of su + hadayaṃ. The variant suhaddayaṃ in the text. In the verse, part of the phrase 'make friends and companions'.
suhaddayañca.example_1: 56. Mittañca kayirātha suhadayañca [suhaddayañca (sī.), sakhāgharañca (pī.)], ayirañca kayirātha sukhāgamāya;
suhaddayañca.translation_1: One should make friends and companions, and one should make a noble one for the sake of happiness;

kojova.meaning_2: like a blanket; like a carpet
kojova.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading of nivatthakocova in the same verse; the text prints kojova, with kojo (nom. sg. of kojava) + va (iva).
kojova.example_1: Nivatthakocova [kojova (sī. pī.)] sarebhihantvā, modāma puttehi samaṅgibhūtā.
kojova.translation_1: Like one who has put on clothes, after having conquered, we rejoice, united with our children.

evaṃkaro.meaning_2: one who acts thus; doing like this; acting in this way
evaṃkaro.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text evaṃkaro is nominative singular masculine, used substantively of a person (brāhmaṇo, samaṇo, macco).
evaṃkaro.example_1: Evaṃkaro brāhmaṇo hoti khemī, dhamme ṭhitaṃ tena amāpayiṃsu.
evaṃkaro.translation_1: One who does this is a brahmin and is peaceful; they said he is firm in Dhamma.
evaṃkaro.example_2: Samaṇo caraṃ hitvā mamāyitāni, evaṃkaro saggamupeti ṭhānaṃ.
evaṃkaro.translation_2: A samaṇa, conducting himself having abandoned attachments, one who acts thus achieves the heavenly mansion.

gharamāvasātu.meaning_2: dwells at home; remains in the house
gharamāvasātu.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of gharaṃ + āvasati. In the text the phrase apassaṃ gharamāvasātu is an optative or imperative wish: 'may he dwell at home not seeing (his own aging)'. The form appears to be āvasātu (3rd sg. imperative/optative of āvasati), though written without the initial ā after gharaṃ.
gharamāvasātu.example_2: Vayaṃ apassaṃ gharamāvasātu, bhisāni te brāhmaṇa yo ahāsi.
gharamāvasātu.translation_2: May he dwell at home not seeing his own aging, he who stole your lotus-roots, Brahmin.

mahimāvasātu.meaning_2: may he rule the earth; may he inhabit the earth
mahimāvasātu.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of mahimaṃ (locative of mahī, 'earth') and avasātu, 3rd singular imperative of avasati in the sense of ruling or inhabiting; the sandhi is unusual and the reading may be corrupt. Alternatively the first element could be mahiṃ with -a- before vasātu.
mahimāvasātu.example_2: Sa cāturantaṃ mahimāvasātu, bhisāni te brāhmaṇa yo ahāsi.
mahimāvasātu.translation_2: May he rule the earth to its four ends, he who stole your lotus-roots, Brahmin.

carātu.meaning_2: let him walk; let him go; let him practice
carātu.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Imperative 3rd singular of carati, used three times in the verse with the sense 'let it go' or 'let him roam'. The form is carātu, with the imperative ending -tu.

bajjhatū.meaning_2: is bound; is tied; is attached (to); is caught (by)
bajjhatū.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Imperative 3rd singular (bajjhatū) in the text, expressing a wish. √bandh with the ya sign gives bajjha-.
bajjhatū.example_2: 89. So bajjhatū pāsasatehi chabbhi [chamhi (sī. pī.), chassu (?)], rammā vanā niyyatu rājadhāniṃ [rājaṭhāniṃ (ka.)];
bajjhatū.translation_2: May he be bound by six-fold ropes and led from the pleasant forest to the capital city;

rājaṭhāniṃ.meaning_2: capital city; royal seat; king's residence
rājaṭhāniṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading of rājadhānī (see Sinhalese edition; also printed rājadhāniṃ). Accusative singular in the verse, after niyyatu. Compound of rāja + ṭhānī, from √ṭhā, but treated as a compound, so root fields are empty.
rājaṭhāniṃ.example_1: 89. So bajjhatū pāsasatehi chabbhi [chamhi (sī. pī.), chassu (?)], rammā vanā niyyatu rājadhāniṃ [rājaṭhāniṃ (ka.)];
rājaṭhāniṃ.translation_1: May he be bound by six-fold ropes and led from the pleasant forest to the capital city;

vupatthambha.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of vi + upatthambha (vi + u > vu). Locative singular in the verse, meaning 'on what ground / with what support'. Sometimes analysed as a contraction of upatthambha.
vupatthambha.example_2: Kismiṃ vupatthambha sahassanetta, isīhi tvaṃ kīḷasi devarāja.
vupatthambha.translation_2: On what grounds, O Thousand-Eyed one, do you play with ascetics, O King of Gods?

dhammacāriṇī.meaning_2: acting in accordance with the Dhamma; practising the Dhamma; righteous
dhammacāriṇī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Feminine form dhammacāriṇī in the text, nominative singular. The separation is dhamma + cārī (from √car 1).
dhammacāriṇī.translation_1: I, finding delight in non-violence, am a follower of the Dhamma;

samacāriṇī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Feminine form of samacārin; nominative singular modifying a woman, used of a faithful wife in the verse. Sometimes spelled samacārinī.
samacāriṇī.example_1: 122. Itthiyo [itthiyā (pī.)] jīvalokasmiṃ, yā hoti [honti (sī. syā.)] samacārinī [samacāriṇī (sī.)];
samacāriṇī.translation_1: In the world of living beings, a woman who is a faithful wife,

kapotiyā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] The form kapotiyā in the text is either instrumental singular ('by/with the female pigeon') or dative/genitive singular ('for/of the female pigeon'), depending on interpretation; the commentary-style gloss takes it as 'consumed by desire for'.
kapotiyā.example_2: 128. Ahaṃ pure giddhigato kapotiyā, asmiṃ padesasmimubho ramāma;
kapotiyā.translation_2: “I was formerly consumed by desire for a female pigeon; in this place we both delighted.

kapotiṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Feminine of kapota. Accusative singular in the text (kapotiṃ).
kapotiṃ.example_2: Athaggahī sākuṇiko kapotiṃ, akāmako tāya vinā ahosiṃ.
kapotiṃ.translation_2: Then a fowler caught the female pigeon; against my will, I was without her.”

kanditva.meaning_2: having cried; having wailed; having lamented
kanditva.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Absolutive in -tvā, written kanditva (shortened final vowel) in the verse. Used with roditvā in the sentence.
kanditva.example_1: 132. Tato janā nikkhamitvāna gāmā, kanditvā roditvā [kanditva roditva (sī.)] apakkamiṃsu;
kanditva.translation_1: “Then the people, having come out from the village, having lamented and wept, departed.

sosayuṃ.meaning_2: causes to dry up; makes dry; dries up
sosayuṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Causative of sussati. In the text the aorist 3rd plural sosayuṃ is used: 'they dried up'.
sosayuṃ.example_2: Uṇho ca vāto tikhiṇā ca rasmiyo, te sosayuṃ tassa karīsamaggaṃ.
sosayuṃ.translation_2: The hot wind and the sharp rays [of the sun] dried up the passage for excrement.

temayī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Aorist 3rd singular of the causative temeti. The PEU entry temayī = [timu+ṇaya+ī] supports the analysis as a causative aorist; so temayī tassa karīsamaggaṃ = "it moistened his excrement path".
temayī.example_2: Mahā ca megho sahasā pavassi, so temayī tassa karīsamaggaṃ.
temayī.translation_2: A vast cloud rained down suddenly; it moistened that passage for excrement.

nikkhamisaṃ.meaning_2: will go out (from); will leave; will depart (from)
nikkhamisaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] First person singular future in -issaṃ of the nikkhamati series, meaning 'I will go out (from)'. Cando yathā rāhumukhā pamutto is a simile for being released.
nikkhamisaṃ.example_2: 136. Tato ahaṃ nikkhamisaṃ bhadante, cando yathā rāhumukhā pamutto;
nikkhamisaṃ.translation_2: Then I exited, Venerable Sir, like the moon released from the jaws of Rahu.

kipillikāni.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] The text has the plural kipillikāni (ni-nighaṇḍu); nominative/accusative plural of an a-stem.
kipillikāni.example_2: 137. Vammīkathūpasmiṃ kipillikāni, nippothayanto tuvaṃ pure carāsi;
kipillikāni.translation_2: “You used to roam around destroying the ants on the ant-hill.

paripothayiṃsu.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Aorist 3rd plural (paripothayiṃsu) in both verses, with patient maṃ; causative of pari + √puṭh, 'struck on all sides'.
paripothayiṃsu.example_2: Tato janā nikkhamitvāna gāmā, kodaṇḍakena paripothayiṃsu maṃ.
paripothayiṃsu.translation_2: Then the people, having come out from the village, beat me with bows.

bandhitva.meaning_2: having tied; having bound; having caught; having formed
bandhitva.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Written bandhitva in the text, a variant of bandhitvā; sandhi with the following morādhipatiṃ in the verse.
bandhitva.example_1: Bandhitvā [bandhitva (sī. pī.)] morādhipatiṃ yasassiṃ, dukkhā sa pamucci [dukkhā pamucci (sī.), dukkhā pamuñci (syā. pī.)] yathāhaṃ pamuttoti.
bandhitva.translation_1: The glorious lord of peacocks he set free From pain, as soon as he was caught, like me.

nitāḷeti.meaning_2: strikes down; beats down; knocks down
nitāḷeti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the first sentence 'tañca seno nitāḷeti' the hawk is the agent ('the hawk strikes that one'). PEU analysis ni + taḷa + ṇe + ti agrees, though the vowel is lengthened before the causative suffix.
nitāḷeti.example_2: Tañca seno nitāḷeti, veyyagghiyeva sā gati.
nitāḷeti.translation_2: The hawk strikes that one; such is the way of the tiger.

appodavaṇṇe.meaning_2: of the appearance of waterless rice-gruel; pale like waterless milk-rice; (of food) of plain colour, unappetising-looking
appodavaṇṇe.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Descriptive compound of appa (little, without) + uda (water) + vaṇṇa (colour, appearance); the PEU splits it as appoda + vaṇṇa. In the verse it agrees with kummāse (masculine accusative plural), describing thick rice-gruel of plain appearance.
appodavaṇṇe.example_2: Appodavaṇṇe kummāse, siṅgiṃ vidalasūpiyo [siṅgiṃ bidalasūpiyo (sī. pī.), siṅgīveraṃ lasūpiyo (ka.) siṅgīnti siṅgīverādikaṃ uttaribhaṅgaṃ; vidalasūpiyoti muggasūpādayo (aṭṭha.) vidalaṃ kalāyādimhi vattatīti sakkatābhidhāne].
appodavaṇṇe.translation_2: Thick porridge, ginger, lentil soup and many other things.

siṅgīnti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Accusative singular in the verse. The commentary glosses siṅgiṃ with siṅgivera, ginger. The -ti is the quotation particle.
siṅgīnti.example_1: Appodavaṇṇe kummāse, siṅgiṃ vidalasūpiyo [siṅgiṃ bidalasūpiyo (sī. pī.), siṅgīveraṃ lasūpiyo (ka.) siṅgīnti siṅgīverādikaṃ uttaribhaṅgaṃ; vidalasūpiyoti muggasūpādayo (aṭṭha.) vidalaṃ kalāyādimhi vattatīti sakkatābhidhāne].
siṅgīnti.translation_1: Thick porridge, ginger, lentil soup and many other things.

vidalaṃ.meaning_2: split pulse; chopped beans (esp. mung beans); pieces of split bean
vidalaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the verse it occurs in the compound vidalasūpiyo (accusative singular before sūpiyo?). The commentary glosses vidalasūpādayo as muggasūpādayo, i.e. bean soup and the like.
vidalaṃ.example_1: Appodavaṇṇe kummāse, siṅgiṃ vidalasūpiyo [siṅgiṃ bidalasūpiyo (sī. pī.), siṅgīveraṃ lasūpiyo (ka.) siṅgīnti siṅgīverādikaṃ uttaribhaṅgaṃ; vidalasūpiyoti muggasūpādayo (aṭṭha.) vidalaṃ kalāyādimhi vattatīti sakkatābhidhāne].
vidalaṃ.translation_1: Thick porridge, ginger, lentil soup and many other things.

paṭiyāni.meaning_2: response; counter-present; return gift; something given in return
paṭiyāni.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Appears in a list of valuable items in a Jātaka verse; probably a gift given in return or a matching present. Doubtful: could be read as paṭi + yāna (a return journey) or as a variant of paṭiyāṇa (a belt or ornament).
paṭiyāni.translation_2: Silver in handfuls, precious rugs, and jewels manifold;

uddiyāni.meaning_2: fringed (blankets); with fringes at both ends
uddiyāni.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Adjective agreeing with kambalā (neuter plural) in the verse; not a headword by itself. The dictionary form is uddiya (PEU: uddiya, from ubhaya + dasā, 'fringed at both ends'). Spelling variant uddiyāne in some editions.
uddiyāni.example_2: 192. Kāsikāni ca vatthāni, uddiyāni ca kambalā [uddiyāne ca kambale (sī. pī.)];
uddiyāni.translation_2: And robes of fine Benares cloth, and blankets thick and thin.

uddiyāne.meaning_2: blanket with fringes on both ends; double-fringed woollen blanket
uddiyāne.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] The text reads uddiyāni (nominative plural) beside kambalā; some editions have uddiyāne. PEU suggests a derivation ubhaya + dasā, but the form is doubtful. Likely a kind of blanket.
uddiyāne.example_1: 192. Kāsikāni ca vatthāni, uddiyāni ca kambalā [uddiyāne ca kambale (sī. pī.)];
uddiyāne.translation_1: And robes of fine Benares cloth, and blankets thick and thin.

nāridā.meaning_2: giving women; bestowing maidens (said of a tree branch)
nāridā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] A poetic compound describing the western branch as giving/bestowing beautiful women (nāri + √dā). Occurs only in this verse; the related entry analyses it as nāri + dā + a, a ti-stem adjective. Nominative singular in the text.
nāridā.example_2: Nāridā pacchimā sākhā, sabbakāme ca uttarā;
nāridā.translation_2: The western gave us pretty maids, the northern all things good:

mādīnavaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In mādīnavaṃ the sandhi is eta + idaṃ > etaṃ, but metrically the vowel is lengthened as etā, then elided to mā before ādīnavaṃ. The word is the genitive plural of eta, "of these (evils)"; the lines read etaṃ ādīnavaṃ, "this danger". The first pāda scans evaṃ (so the variant eta matches). Alternative analysis: mā + ādīnavaṃ, "the danger of Māra".
mādīnavaṃ.example_1: 201. Eva [eta (sī. pī.)] mādīnavaṃ ñatvā, taṇhā dukkhassa sambhavaṃ;
mādīnavaṃ.translation_1: So let him, seeing this evil thing, pain rooted in desire,

sādhīno.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Proper name of the king of Mithilā; variant reading sādhino in the text. The PEU splits it as sa + adhīna, but as a name the compound analysis is doubtful.
sādhīno.example_1: 205. Tato ca rājā sādhino [sādhīno (sī. pī.)], vedeho mithilaggaho [pamukho rathamāruhi (sī. pī.)];
sādhīno.translation_1: 205. Then King Sādhina, the ruler of Mithilā, of Videha, mounted the vehicle;

cāhametamicchāmi.grammar: sandhi, ind + pron + pron + pron + pr
cāhametamicchāmi.meaning_2: and I do not desire this
cāhametamicchāmi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of ca + ahaṃ + etaṃ + na + icchāmi (na + icchāmi contracted to micchāmi with sandhi). Found in Jātaka verse 213.
cāhametamicchāmi.translation_2: 213. 'I do not desire this which comes from a gift from another;

vaname.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] The text form vaname is probably vanaṃ + e or a mis-segmentation of vanamige; if it is really vana + e it is a separate sandhi form. The PEU entries point to vana + miga.

viciya.meaning_2: having investigated; having examined; having analysed; having discerned
viciya.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading (ka.) for vicayaṃ in the verse; the same form would be absolutive of vicināti. The commentary reading is vicayaṃ, a noun in apposition.
viciya.example_1: Tesaṃ vibhaṅgaṃ vicayaṃ [viciya (ka.)], vitthārena suṇohi me.
viciya.translation_1: Listen to me as I explain their classification in detail.

ambajambuvibhīṭakaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of three fruit names (amba, jambu, vibhītaka) in the verse; the Burmese and Sinhalese editions read them separately. Accusative singular in the text.
ambajambuvibhīṭakaṃ.example_1: 242. Harītakaṃ [harīṭakaṃ (bahūsu)] āmalakaṃ, ambaṃ jambuṃ vibhītakaṃ [ambajambuvibhīṭakaṃ (sī. pī.)];
ambajambuvibhīṭakaṃ.translation_1: Myrobalan, gooseberry, mango, rose-apple, belleric myrobalan,

aṇḍacchedā.meaning_2: castrator; one who cuts off the testicles
aṇḍacchedā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text a nominative plural in -ā, agreeing with nilañchakā. The related form aṇḍacchedaka is an adjective.
aṇḍacchedā.example_2: Bahū te [ne (syā. ka.)] paripucchanti, aṇḍacchedā nilañchakā [tilañchakā (pī.)].
aṇḍacchedā.translation_2: They question many people, they are gelded and marked.

āgodhā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the Jātaka verse paired with macchakacchapaṃ; possibly a lizard (iguana). The vowel of the final member appears shortened from godhā in the compound.
āgodhā.translation_2: They bind hares and cats, and hunt lizards, fish, and tortoises.

mupocitaṃ.meaning_2: and honoured; and served; and waited upon
mupocitaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Probably sandhi of mu (variant of pi/su, emphatic) + upocitaṃ, pp of upa + √ci in the sense 'honoured; served'. The alternative reading mupocitaṃ with gloss (bahūsu) suggests uncertainty; it may instead be muditaṃ ('pleased') or a compound reading 'by many honoured'. Instrumental/locative context in the verse.
mupocitaṃ.translation_1: Endowed with the best gabled cells, and waited upon with a magnificent seat.

āmantaṇīyo.meaning_2: to be invited; to be addressed; to be spoken to
āmantaṇīyo.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Spelling āmantaṇīyo in the text (āmantanīyo in other editions). Nominative singular of the potential participle, agreeing with the subject.
āmantaṇīyo.example_1: Garu ca āmantanīyo [āmantaṇīyo (sī. pī.)] ca, dātumarahāmi bhojanaṃ.
āmantaṇīyo.translation_1: He is respected and to be invited, I ought to give the food to him.

biḷālitakkaḷāni.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Plural form biḷālitakkaḷāni in the text. Probably a compound of biḷāli (?) and takkaḷa (radish).
biḷālitakkaḷāni.example_1: 280. Khaṇantālukalambāni [khaṇamālukalambāni (syā. ka.)], bilālitakkalāni ca [biḷālitakkaḷāni ca (sī. pī.)];
biḷālitakkaḷāni.translation_1: Digging up bulbs and radishes, and lotus stalks;

saṃhāriyaṃ.meaning_2: to be gathered together; to be collected; to be drawn together
saṃhāriyaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Potential participle (gerundive) in -ya of saṃharati; variant reading, the text's saṅghāriyaṃ is a scribal variant. Accusative singular neuter agreeing with sāmākanīvāraṃ; the sense 'gathering (millet and wild rice)' fits the verse.
saṃhāriyaṃ.example_1: Dhunaṃ sāmākanīvāraṃ, saṅghāriyaṃ pasāriyaṃ [saṃhāriyaṃ pahāriyaṃ (syā.), saṃsāriyaṃ pasāriyaṃ (ka.)].
saṃhāriyaṃ.translation_1: Shaking out millet and wild rice, gathering and spreading them.

kharājinaso.meaning_2: with a black leopard's hide; covered with a dark antelope skin
kharājinaso.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Appears in a Jātaka verse list of names; probably a name or epithet (Kharājina). Vocative or nominative singular in the text; if read as khara + ajina + so, it is two words joined by sandhi.
kharājinaso.example_2: Suva kinnara mukka kharājinaso, bhisajāta mahesi kapotavaro;
kharājinaso.translation_2: Suva, Kinnara, Mukka, Kharājina, So, Bhisajāta, Mahesi, Kapotavaro;

māsasānā.meaning_2: hoping for fruit in a month; looking forward to fruit after a month
māsasānā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading of māsasānā (Sinhalese and PTS editions) for māsiṃ samānā (Burmese edition); a compound of māsa (month) + sāna (from √san, seeking), nominative plural agreeing with the sowers. The text's reading is māsasānā, so the lemma may also be taken as māsasāna.
māsasānā.example_1: 4. Thale ca ninne ca vapanti bījaṃ, anūpakhette phalamāsamānā [māsasānā (sī. pī.), māsiṃ samānā (syā.)];
māsasānā.translation_1: They sow seeds on high ground and in hollows, hoping for fruit in the marshy fields.

māsiṃ.meaning_2: monthly; every month; for a month
māsiṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the verse, māsiṃ appears in the phrase anūpakhette phalamāsamānā, where it may mean 'monthly' or 'for a month'. The text is uncertain, and the variant māsiṃ samānā may reflect a different parsing. The reading is not fully settled.
māsiṃ.example_1: 4. Thale ca ninne ca vapanti bījaṃ, anūpakhette phalamāsamānā [māsasānā (sī. pī.), māsiṃ samānā (syā.)];
māsiṃ.translation_1: They sow seeds on high ground and in hollows, hoping for fruit in the marshy fields.

upajotiyo.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] A proper name in the Jātaka verse, probably one of four gatekeepers (with Upajjhāya and Gandakucchi). Nominative singular upajotiyo in the text.
upajotiyo.example_2: 8. Kvettha gatā [kvattha gatā (syā.), kattheva bhaṭṭhā (pī.)] upajotiyo ca, upajjhāyo ca athavā gaṇḍakucchi [aṇḍakucchi (sī. syā. pī.)];
upajotiyo.translation_2: Where have those gatekeepers, Upajotiya, Upajjhaya, and Gandhakucchi gone?

aṇḍakucchi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] A proper name in the text, variant reading of gaṇḍakucchi; nominative singular in the verse.
aṇḍakucchi.example_1: 8. Kvettha gatā [kvattha gatā (syā.), kattheva bhaṭṭhā (pī.)] upajotiyo ca, upajjhāyo ca athavā gaṇḍakucchi [aṇḍakucchi (sī. syā. pī.)];
aṇḍakucchi.translation_1: Where have those gatekeepers, Upajotiya, Upajjhaya, and Gandhakucchi gone?

mahakkasāvesu.meaning_2: with great impurity; greatly stained (with defilements); deeply depraved
mahakkasāvesu.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Bahubbīhi compound: mahant + kasāva, 'having great stains (of defilements)'. Locative plural in the text. The PEU entry is confused.
mahakkasāvesu.translation_2: you give gifts to those who are of great impurity, to those who are evildoers and intemperate.

paṭigāya.meaning_2: sings back; recites in response; receives by singing
paṭigāya.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Imperative 2nd singular in the text (paṭigāhi is a variant reading). The prefix paṭi here means 'back, in return'.
paṭigāya.example_1: ‘‘ Gantvāna rañño paṭigāhi [paṭigāyi (syā. ka.), paṭigāya (?)] gāthaṃ, api te varaṃ attamano dadeyya ’’[api nu te varaṃ attamano dadeyya (syā.), api nu te attamano varaṃ dade (ka.)].
paṭigāya.translation_1: “Go and receive the verse from the king, and he might give you a reward, being pleased.”

paṭisaṃyamissaṃ.meaning_2: restrains oneself; controls oneself; guards oneself
paṭisaṃyamissaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Future first person singular in the text (paṭisaṃyamissaṃ = paṭisaṃyamissati). The PEU splits it as pati + saṃ + yamu + ssaṃ, future of paṭisaṃyamati.
paṭisaṃyamissaṃ.example_2: Attānameva paṭisaṃyamissaṃ, na patthaye putta [puttaṃ (sī. pī.)] pasuṃ dhanaṃ vā.
paṭisaṃyamissaṃ.translation_2: I will restrain myself; I do not desire sons, cattle, or wealth.

byasanno.meaning_2: sinking; sinking down; sunk; despairing; despondent
byasanno.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Past participle of visīdati (via sandhi vi + asanna). In the verses it describes one sunk or stuck in mud and in the mire of sensual desire. Nominative singular.

mupeti.grammar: pr, 3rd sing of upeti; variant reading for upehi
mupeti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading (pī. ka.) for upehi in the second verse; the prefix upa- has assimilated to mu-. The first verse also has an uncertain mupeti. Probably an unusual spelling of upeti; the stem follows the eti pattern.
mupeti.example_2: Datvā ca bhutvā ca yathānubhāvaṃ, anindito saggamupehi [mupeti (pī. ka.)] ṭhānaṃ.
mupeti.translation_2: And having given and partaken according to your power, go to heaven, blameless.

manasī.meaning_2: in mind; mentally; (with karoti) to keep in mind; to pay attention to
manasī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Used in the phrase manasī karohi 'keep in mind; pay attention'. Possibly an absolutive-like or adverbial form of manas (locative manasi with lengthened final vowel for the metre); treated here as an indeclinable.
manasī.example_2: Imameva gāthaṃ manasī karohi, bhāsesi [bhāsehi (syā. pī. ka.)] cenaṃ parisāya majjhe.
manasī.translation_2: Keep this very verse in mind, and speak it in the midst of the assembly:

vajantyā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Feminine present participle in instrumental singular, agreeing with a female animal in the verse; the form is vajantyā.
vajantyā.translation_2: A person who slept in the open, nursed while walking, and surrounded by dogs,

māgatosi.meaning_2: you have not come here; haven't you come here
māgatosi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of na + āgato + asi (na + āgata > māgata; āgata (pp of āgacchati) + asi (pr of √as)). Negative interrogative in the verse; 'māgato' is also a common word (the Magadha people), but that does not fit here. Respelled in the text as māgatosi.
māgatosi.example_2: 53. Kenānusiṭṭho idha māgatosi, vanibbaka [vaṇibbaka (sī.)] cakkhupathāni yācituṃ;
māgatosi.translation_2: By whom were you instructed, mendicant, to come here to ask for the path of the eyes?

cakkhupathāni.meaning_2: path of the eye; range of vision; something worth seeing; a sight for the eyes
cakkhupathāni.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Plural accusative cakkhupathāni here in the sense of things worthy to be seen, i.e. eyes. Part of a compound: cakkhupathāni yācituṃ.

māgatosmi.meaning_2: I am like a beast; I am a wild animal
māgatosmi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of māga (beast) + to (like, as) + asmi (I am). Occurs in a Jātaka verse; the exact segmentation is uncertain, possibly māga + to + asmi or māga + ato + asmi.
māgatosmi.example_2: Tenānusiṭṭho idha māgatosmi, vanibbako cakkhupathāni yācituṃ.
māgatosmi.translation_2: Instructed by him, I have come here, a mendicant, to ask for the path of the eyes.

tadate.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Probably a sandhi of tad (that) + te (to you), so "that (is) for you". The PEU suggests tadattha, but the context (yadicchase tvaṃ tadate samijjhatu) points to a sandhi. Doubtful; requires checking against the commentary.
tadate.example_2: Sa cakkhumā gaccha janassa pekkhato, yadicchase tvaṃ tadate samijjhatu.
tadate.translation_2: Go as one with vision in the view of the people, may that which you desire be accomplished for you.

parikkari.meaning_2: please do not; do not treat (us) thus
parikkari.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading (ka.) in the verse; the editors explain it as pari + ā + kari, a negated aorist of karoti with the prohibitive mā. The main reading is parākari, identical in meaning here.
parikkari.example_1: 58. Mā no deva adā cakkhuṃ, mā no sabbe parākari [parakkari (syā. ka. aṭṭha.), parikkari (ka.) pari + ā + kari = parākari];
parikkari.translation_1: Do not give the eye, O lord, do not do this to us;

sīviyo.meaning_2: Sivi; name of a people; one of the Sivis
sīviyo.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] The text reads sīviyo, with the variant sivayo; nominative plural, referring to the Sivi people in the Jātaka verse.
sīviyo.example_1: 60. Yathā taṃ sivayo [sīviyo (syā.)] sabbe, sayoggā sarathā sadā;
sīviyo.translation_1: Just as all the Sivis, always with vehicles and chariots;

uddhatva.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant absolutive of uddharati; the commentary glosses it as uddharitvā. In the verse: having pulled out my eyes for the mendicant who desires them.
uddhatva.example_1: Uddharitvā [uddhatva (sī.), laddha tvaṃ (pī.)] cakkhūni mamaṃ jigīsato, hatthesu ṭhapehi [āvesi (sī.)] vanibbakassa.
uddhatva.translation_1: Having pulled out my eyes for the one who desires them, place them in the hands of the mendicant.

āvesi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Aorist 2nd singular of āvisati, used as an imperative in this verse. The PeU gloss āvesaka ("joined in") supports the same root. Some editions read āvesi as a short form of āvesehi.
āvesi.example_1: Uddharitvā [uddhatva (sī.), laddha tvaṃ (pī.)] cakkhūni mamaṃ jigīsato, hatthesu ṭhapehi [āvesi (sī.)] vanibbakassa.
āvesi.translation_1: Having pulled out my eyes for the one who desires them, place them in the hands of the mendicant.

uddhatvā.meaning_2: having pulled out; having plucked out; having drawn out; having extracted
uddhatvā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Absolutive of uddharati (ud + √har, 'to lift up, draw out, pull out'). The text's variant uddharitvā confirms the reading; the form uddhatvā shows the contraction of -ari- to -a- before -tvā. Used here of pulling out the king's eyes.
uddhatvā.translation_1: Having pulled out the king's eyes, he offered them to the brahmin;

uparūḷhesu.meaning_2: healed; grown back; restored; (of eyes) recovered
uparūḷhesu.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Locative plural in the text: 'when the eyes had healed'. From upa + √ruh 'grow up'; the pp rūḷha with the prefix upa giving the sense of recovery to a normal state.
uparūḷhesu.translation_2: Then, after a few days, when the eyes had healed;

nīdha.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] The form nīdha occurs in Jātaka verse, apparently as an indeclinable meaning 'here' or 'now'. Its analysis is uncertain; it may be a sandhi or a rare particle. The related PEU entry nīgha is different.

vidadhāti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] 3rd singular present of vidadhāti (vi + √dhā). In the verse it means 'produces (wealth)'. The PEU entry suggests 'arrange and reform'.
vidadhāti.example_2: 87. Na sippametaṃ vidadhāti bhogaṃ, na bandhuvā [na bandhavā (sī. syā. ka.)] na sarīravaṇṇo yo [na sarīrāvakāso (sī. syā. pī.)];
vidadhāti.translation_2: “This skill does not produce wealth, nor do relatives, nor one's bodily appearance;

gorimandaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading at Ja 6 verse; the accepted text has goravindaṃ (probably go + ravinda, 'cow-lotus', i.e. a cowherd? or 'chief of cows'). Accusative singular in the sentence.
gorimandaṃ.example_1: Passeḷamūgaṃ sukhamedhamānaṃ, sirī hi naṃ bhajate goravindaṃ [gorimandaṃ (sī. pī.)];
gorimandaṃ.translation_1: Look at the mute prospering in happiness; for wealth visits the cowherd.

samabhicaranti.meaning_2: surrounds; gathers around; approaches from all sides
samabhicaranti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading of samabhisaranti (√sar) in the verse. Present 3rd plural in the text.
samabhicaranti.example_1: 89. Dumaṃ yathā sāduphalaṃ araññe, samantato samabhisaranti [samabhicaranti (sī. pī.)] pakkhī;
samabhicaranti.translation_1: “Just as birds flock from all sides to a tree in the forest that has sweet fruit;

sabbakālamasaṅkhyaṃ.meaning_2: at all times without number; at all times uncountable
sabbakālamasaṅkhyaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of sabbakālaṃ (adverb, 'at all times') and asaṅkhyaṃ (adjective qualifying najjo, 'numberless'). Sometimes analysed as a compound, but the separate words are commoner; the form as it stands may be retained as a sandhi entry.
sabbakālamasaṅkhyaṃ.example_2: 92. Yametamakkhā udadhiṃ mahantaṃ, savanti najjo sabbakālamasaṅkhyaṃ;
sabbakālamasaṅkhyaṃ.translation_2: “The rivers flow into this great ocean, which I describe, at all times, without number;

saṃvidheti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] 3rd singular present of saṃvidheti (causative of saṃvidahati). The form vidhe- represents the causative stem. Some grammars derive it from √dhā with the causative suffix -e, giving saṃvidheti; others relate it to √dhā with a different strengthening. The meaning 'arranges' fits the context.
saṃvidheti.example_2: Yaṃ paṇḍito nipuṇaṃ saṃvidheti, sammohamāpajjati tattha bālo;
saṃvidheti.translation_2: Whatever the wise person arranges with skill, the fool falls into confusion there;

mākaṅkhi.meaning_2: do not doubt; do not hesitate; do not wish
mākaṅkhi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Prohibitive (mā + present 3rd singular); sandhi of mā + kaṅkhati. Also analysed as mā + kaṅkhī (2nd singular). The line 'gaccha tuvampi mākaṅkhi' means 'go, and you too do not hesitate'.
mākaṅkhi.example_2: Gaccha tuvampi mākaṅkhi, jīvissanti tayā saha.
mākaṅkhi.translation_2: Go thou with them, and linger not, for they shall live with thee.”

ṭhāpasa.meaning_2: established; placed; set up; laid down
ṭhāpasa.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Text variant in the Jātaka verse (syā. ka.) for the reading of the verb; likely aorist 2nd singular ṭhāpesi, a causative form of √ṭhā. The printed text has ṭhāpasa, perhaps an alternative 2nd singular aorist ending -asa, or a misreading. Uncertain.
ṭhāpasa.example_1: 158. Etaṃ me upamaṃ katvā, putte vijjāsu vācaya [ṭhāpasa (syā. ka.)];
ṭhāpasa.translation_1: “By using this similitude all wisdom’s truths explain,

lohituṇhīso.meaning_2: having a red turban; wearing a red headdress
lohituṇhīso.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Bahubbīhi compound describing a king. Nominative singular in the verse.
lohituṇhīso.translation_2: Shines with a red turban, shining like the sun during the day.

vijigucchase.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] 2nd singular present of vijigucchati, a desiderative/causative formation from √gup 1. In the text it means 'do you despise (it)?'.
vijigucchase.example_2: Mātari mayhaṃ naggāya, kinnu tvaṃ vijigucchase.
vijigucchase.translation_2: Why do you despise the calling we live by, when my mother is naked?

tomarāni.meaning_2: spear; javelin; two-pronged spear (used against elephants)
tomarāni.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Neuter plural in the text (tomarāni ca) in a list of weapons; often masc. in commentaries.
tomarāni.translation_2: Take up the bows, the javelins and the spears;

visīlaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Accusative singular in the text, agreeing with the noun it qualifies. Negated adjective of sīla.
visīlaṃ.example_2: Sīlavantaṃ visīlaṃ vā, vasaṃ tasseva gacchati.
visīlaṃ.translation_2: Whether virtuous or without virtue—one comes under his sway.

nopaseveyya.meaning_2: should not associate (with); should not keep company (with)
nopaseveyya.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] na + upaseveyya (optative of upasevati, √sev). Sandhi of na + u- as no-.
nopaseveyya.translation_2: The learned one should not associate with the bad, but should associate with the good;

bhallāṭiyo.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Proper name; variant reading bhallātiyo in some editions. Nominative singular in the verse.
bhallāṭiyo.example_1: 186. Bhallātiyo [bhallāṭiyo (sī. pī.)] nāma ahosi rājā, raṭṭhaṃ pahāya migavaṃ acāri so;
bhallāṭiyo.translation_1: There was a king named Bhallatiya, who, having abandoned his realm, practiced hunting.

sāḷūrasaṅghañca.meaning_2: pack of dogs; group of hounds
sāḷūrasaṅghañca.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text joined with -ca (sāḷūrasaṅghañca); accusative singular, object of nisedhayitvā. The DPD PEU guide gives sāḷūra as "dog" here, though it is normally a kind of dog or jackal.
sāḷūrasaṅghañca.example_2: 187. Sāḷūrasaṅghañca nisedhayitvā, dhanuṃ [dhanu (sī. syā. pī.)] kalāpañca so nikkhipitvā;
sāḷūrasaṅghañca.translation_2: Having quieted his pack of hounds, and having laid down his bow and quiver,

sītodiyā.meaning_2: having cool water; with cold water (name of a river)
sītodiyā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant sītodiyā in the text (Sinhalese and PTS editions), for sītodakā; here a river name or epithet of rivers, ablative/genitive singular or nominative plural.
sītodiyā.example_1: 189. Mallaṃ giriṃ paṇḍarakaṃ tikūṭaṃ, sītodakā [sītodiyā (sī. pī.), sītodikā (?)] anuvicarāma najjo;
sītodiyā.translation_1: “We wander through the Malla, Paṇḍaraka, and Tikūṭa mountains, and the rivers with cool water.

sattaliyothikañca.meaning_2: name of a flower (possibly a kind of jasmine or water lily)
sattaliyothikañca.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text sattaliyothikañca is a sandhi compound of sattali + yothikaṃ + ca; the entry is for the first element sattali, a noun used in a list of flowers.
sattaliyothikañca.translation_2: “And I was gathering aṅkolaka, atimuttaka, and sattali flowers,

oceyya.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Absolutive form in -eyya, probably metrically shortened for ocayitvā (ava + ci + tvā). The PEU analysis oceyya = ava + ci + tvā agrees in meaning; the ending is irregular. In these verses it describes plucking flowers to make a garland or a burden.

yatthajjamaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of yattha (where) and ajja (today, now); variant yatthajjimaṃ. Part of a clause meaning 'where we will spend the night'.
yatthajjamaṃ.example_1: Idañca no hehiti santharatthaṃ, yatthajjimaṃ [yatthajjamaṃ (sī. pī.)] viharissāma [viharissāmu (pī.)] rattiṃ.
yatthajjamaṃ.translation_1: this will be our bedding, where we will spend the night.”

viharissāmu.meaning_2: will stay; will dwell; will spend (the night)
viharissāmu.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] First person plural future in the text (viharissāmu in some editions for viharissāma).
viharissāmu.example_1: Idañca no hehiti santharatthaṃ, yatthajjimaṃ [yatthajjamaṃ (sī. pī.)] viharissāma [viharissāmu (pī.)] rattiṃ.
viharissāmu.translation_1: this will be our bedding, where we will spend the night.”

akaluṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading akaluṃ (accusative singular) for agaḷuṃ in the verse; a fragrant wood paired with candanaṃ. The PEU entry akalusa (na + kalusa) is a different word.
akaluṃ.example_1: 200. Ahañca kho agaḷuṃ [aggalu (syā. ka.), akaluṃ (pī.)] candanañca, silāya piṃsāmi pamattarūpā;
akaluṃ.translation_1: “And I, being heedless, was pounding eaglewood and sandalwood on a stone,

āliṅgiyā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text the reading is āliṅgiyā, probably a metrical lengthening of āliṅgiya before the caesura; used adverbially with aññamaññaṃ, 'having embraced each other'.
āliṅgiyā.example_2: Āliṅgiyā aññamaññaṃ mayaṃ ubho, sakimpi rodāma sakiṃ hasāma.
āliṅgiyā.translation_2: we both embraced each other, and at times we wept, at times we laughed.”

tīhūnakaṃ.meaning_2: short of three; minus three; less three
tīhūnakaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Adverbial use with a number: 'three less' (sattasatāni tīhūnakaṃ = 703). Instrumental tīhi with ūnakaṃ; sometimes written as a compound adjective.
tīhūnakaṃ.example_2: 204. Tīhūnakaṃ sattasatāni ludda, yamidha mayaṃ vippavasimha pubbe;
tīhūnakaṃ.translation_2: “Seven hundred years and three, huntsman, since we were previously parted,

nvejja.construction: na + u + ajja? or ko + nvejja?
nvejja.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Probably a sandhi of na/ko + u/eva + ajja; uncertain. The commentary glosses ko nvejja seti and ko ajja setu.
nvejja.example_1: Kassajja mātāpitaro rudantu, kvajja setu [ko nvejja seti (ka.), ko ajja setu (?)] nihato pathabyā.
nvejja.translation_1: For whom must mothers and fathers weep today? Who lies here on the ground, destroyed?”

pothayitosmi.meaning_2: is struck; is beaten; is crushed
pothayitosmi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading for heṭhayitosmi in the verse; a passive-causative-looking 1st person singular with the -itosmi ending. Treated here as a present form of pothayati, causative of √puth (crush, strike); the syntax is doubtful.
pothayitosmi.example_1: Ahiṃsako reṇumanuppavissa, puttena te heṭhayitosmi [pothayitosmi (ka.)] deva.
pothayitosmi.translation_1: I am a non-harmer, having entered the dust, yet I have been annoyed by your son, O King.”

āgañchu.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] The text reading āgañchu is probably a variant or metrical form of the aorist 3rd plural āgañchuṃ (the commentary gives āgañchuṃ, the pada text gives āgañchu), from āgacchati. The headword here follows the related PEU entry āgañchi.
āgañchu.example_1: 217. Āgacchuṃ [āgañchuṃ (sī.), āgañchu (pī.)] dovārikā khaggabandhā, kāsāviyā hantu mamaṃ janinda;
āgañchu.translation_1: “The guards with swords have arrived; let the executioners kill me, O King;

pāricaratappamatto.meaning_2: unremitting in tending; diligent in attending (the fire)
pāricaratappamatto.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Compound of pāricara (from pari + car) and appamatta; modifies the implied subject in the verse. Nominative singular.
pāricaratappamatto.example_2: 218. Sāyañca pāto udakaṃ sajāti, aggiṃ sadā pāricaratappamatto;
pāricaratappamatto.translation_2: “Morning and evening he draws water, he tends the fire always, unremittingly;

dunnikkayo.meaning_2: hard to remove; difficult to uproot
dunnikkayo.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Describes a bamboo (veḷu) in Jātaka verse 222; nominative singular in the text.
dunnikkayo.example_2: 222. Daḷhasmi mūle visaṭe virūḷhe, dunnikkayo veḷu pasākhajāto;
dunnikkayo.translation_2: “The root is firm, wide-spread, and grown; the bamboo thicket is hard to remove;

kinnūdha.meaning_2: what now here?; how is it that?
kinnūdha.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of kiṃ nu idha; used rhetorically in verse.
kinnūdha.example_2: 224. Kinnūdha deva tavamatthi bhogā, pubbevahaṃ [pubbe cahaṃ (ka.)] devaloke ramissaṃ;
kinnūdha.translation_2: “What possessions of yours are there here, O King? Previously I enjoyed the heaven of the gods;

vebhaṅgo.meaning_2: failure; spoiling; loss of potency (of medicine)
vebhaṅgo.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text it is nominative singular: bhesajjassa + iva vebhaṅgo, 'like the spoiling of a medicine'. Sandhi of vi + bhaṅga; written with e and aspirate bh.
vebhaṅgo.translation_2: Like the failure of a medicine, its result is bad.”

pabbajjamevābhimanohamasmi.meaning_2: indeed I am inclined only to the going forth; I am only intent on renunciation
pabbajjamevābhimanohamasmi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of pabbajjaṃ (fem acc sg) + eva + abhimanohamasmi (abhi + manohamasmi, 'I am inclined towards'). The long ā is the result of eva + abhi. The whole phrase reads 'I am indeed inclined only towards the going forth'.
pabbajjamevābhimanohamasmi.translation_2: With difficulty I am freed from execution today; I am indeed inclined toward going forth.”

yamuggatejo.meaning_2: whose power is like death; whose fiery energy is like death (an epithet of a snake)
yamuggatejo.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Compound of yama (death) + gata (gone, like) + teja (power). Vocative singular in the verse; also found as yamuggatejo in the text with the nominative sandhi ending.
yamuggatejo.example_2: 243. Yamuggatejo uragoti cāhu, nāgoti naṃ āhu janā janinda;
yamuggatejo.translation_2: “Crawling serpent, fierce as flame! So they called him: one there came,

māgacchi.meaning_2: do not go; did not go; not approach
māgacchi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] For mā agacchi: mā (prohibitive particle) + agacchi (aorist 2nd/3rd singular of gacchati). In the verses it seems to mean 'came' or 'approached', so the negative mā may be questionable.
māgacchi.example_2: 244. Kathaṃ nvayaṃ balaviriyūpapanno, hatthatta [hatthattha (sī. syā. pī.)] māgacchi vanibbakassa;
māgacchi.translation_2: “How could such a starveling wight catch a creature full of might?

dubbissasametamāhu.meaning_2: indeed this is said of the hard-to-believe; truly it is called difficult to trust
dubbissasametamāhu.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Compound-sandhi, tentatively dubbissa + samaṃ + etaṃ + āhu ('truly, this is said to be hard to trust'); dubbissa could also be dubbissā with metrical shortening. Sandhi is uncertain, so the division and pos are open to review.
dubbissasametamāhu.example_2: 254. Addhā hi dubbissasametamāhu, yaṃ mānuso vissase amānusamhi;
dubbissasametamāhu.translation_2: “Superhuman beings may hardly win belief, they say.

tvevahaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of tu (but) + eva (indeed) + ahaṃ (I). Always followed by na ... bhaṇeyyaṃ in these verses: 'but I would not indeed speak a lie'.
tvevahaṃ.example_2: Sabbā ca najjo paṭisotaṃ vajeyyuṃ, na tvevahaṃ rāja musā bhaṇeyyaṃ.
tvevahaṃ.translation_2: Flow upstream the running rivers, I, O King! could never lie.”

saṃvaṭṭeyaṃ.meaning_2: would contract; would dissolve; would roll together
saṃvaṭṭeyaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Optative 3rd singular; the text reads saṃvaṭṭeyaṃ by metrical variation, with sī./pī. adding the -ṃ. Refers to the contraction of the world at the end of the aeon.
saṃvaṭṭeyaṃ.example_1: 256. Nabhaṃ phaleyya udadhīpi susse, saṃvaṭṭaye [saṃvaṭṭeyaṃ (sī. pī.), saṃvaṭṭeyya (syā. ka.)] bhūtadharā vasundharā;
saṃvaṭṭeyaṃ.translation_1: “Split the sky, the sea run dry, bounteous mother earth awry

mubbahe.meaning_2: would break off; would tear out; would uproot
mubbahe.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading (Sinhalese, Syāmarī, Pīṭaka) for muppate (mubbhati, muṭṭhahe is another variant); optative 1st singular in the sentence, used of uprooting Mount Meru.
mubbahe.example_1: Siluccayo meru samūlamuppate [mubbahe (sī. syā. pī. ka. aṭṭha.), muṭṭhahe (ka.)], na tvevahaṃ rāja musā bhaṇeyyaṃ.
mubbahe.translation_1: Crumpling roll, uproot Mount Meru, yet, O King, I could not lie!”

anukampasī.meaning_2: have compassion (for); pity; feel sorry (for); care (for)
anukampasī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] 2nd person singular present of anukampati, addressed to the king (janinda). The PEU entries anukampaka and anukampana are related derivatives.
anukampasī.example_2: 261. Anukampasī nāgakulaṃ janinda, mātā yathā suppiyaṃ ekaputtaṃ;
anukampasī.translation_2: “As a mother would have done to an only well-loved son,

naccayuṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] The text has naccayuṃ, a variant reading of naccisuṃ; both are 3rd plural aorist forms of naccati, meaning 'they danced'. The aorist stem is nacca-.
naccayuṃ.example_1: Dibbā tūriyā pavajjiṃsu, nāgakaññā ca naccisuṃ [naccayuṃ (sī. pī. ka.)].
naccayuṃ.translation_1: Celestial harps made melody, fair serpent-maidens danced.”

sopassaye.meaning_2: with a resting place; with a couch; together with a pillow; furnished with support
sopassaye.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Alternative reading sāpassaye in the text; here the word describes a golden seat with a bolster or resting support. Locative singular in the verse.
sopassaye.translation_1: Where the bevy of fair maidens tread the halls with thronging feet.”

nīrajā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Formed with the negative prefix nī- (= ni-) and raja (dust). In the text it is nominative singular feminine, agreeing with bhūmi ('ground').
nīrajā.example_2: Antepure bhūmiyaṃ santharantu, nikkaddamā hehiti nīrajā ca.
nīrajā.translation_2: Take and spread them in thy palace till nor earth nor dirt be seen.”

bhandhituṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Infinitive with -ituṃ suffix (sandhi -a + i > -i). The text gives bhandhituṃ as a variant reading for bandhituṃ, suggesting a spelling change. Bandhati is the present 3rd singular.
bhandhituṃ.example_1: Bandhi naṃ [bhandhituṃ (syā. ka.)] anupubbena, āraññamiva kuñjaraṃ.
bhandhituṃ.translation_1: she bound him progressively, like a tusker in the forest.

raṭṭhāto.meaning_2: from the realm; from the country; from the kingdom
raṭṭhāto.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Ablative singular in -ā (raṭṭhā), with the emphatic/euphonic -to variant raṭṭhāto in some manuscripts (also raṭṭhato). The text reads samhā raṭṭhā ca khattiyo, "and the aristocrat from the realm".
raṭṭhāto.example_1: 301. Tañca rājā vivāhesi [nivāhesi (syā.), vihāhesi (pī.)], samhā raṭṭhā ca [raṭṭhāto (sī. pī.), raṭṭhato (ka.)] khattiyo;
raṭṭhāto.translation_1: The king banished him and the aristocrat from the realm;

virājayi.meaning_2: abandons; gives up; frees oneself from
virājayi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Aorist 3sg virājayi in the text (with -i for -esi); means 'abandoned, gave up' here, with kāmarāgaṃ as object.
virājayi.translation_2: Then he, having gone forth, abandoned sensual desire;

vāvīkareyya.meaning_2: should one reveal?; should one disclose?
vāvīkareyya.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of vā (or) + vīkareyya, optative of vīkaroti (to reveal, disclose). The variant reading vāvikareyya shows the same sandhi without the lengthened ī. Occurs in the Jātaka verse on revealing secrets.
vāvīkareyya.example_2: Nindiyamatthaṃ pasaṃsiyaṃ vā, kassevāvikareyya [kassa vāvīkareyya (ka.)] guyhamatthaṃ.
vāvīkareyya.translation_2: Whether regarding a blameworthy matter or a praiseworthy one, to whom should one reveal a secret matter?

vāvikareyya.meaning_2: should reveal; should disclose; should make known
vāvikareyya.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Written vāvikareyya, resolved as vā + vikareyya (optative 3rd singular of vikaroti, 'to make manifest'). Alternatively vā + api + kareyya, but the sense 'reveal a secret to a friend' favours vikareyya.
vāvikareyya.example_2: Nindiyamatthaṃ pasaṃsiyaṃ vā, sakhino vāvikareyya guyhamatthaṃ.
vāvikareyya.translation_2: Whether regarding a blameworthy matter or a praiseworthy one, one should reveal a secret matter to a friend.

nipphādā.meaning_2: non-accomplishment; non-completion; state of not being brought about
nipphādā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading in the Jātaka verse; other manuscripts have anipphannatā or anipphādāya. Here it is likely na + nipphādā (a negated abstract noun) taken as an independent feminine in the phrase ā nipphādā. Senses of ṇipphāda (Sanskrit niṣpāda) mean 'accomplishment', so the negated form means 'until non-accomplishment / non-completion'.
nipphādā.example_1: Anipphannatā [anipphādāya (sī. pī.), anipphannatāya (syā.), ā nipphādā (?)] saheyya dhīro, nipphannova [nipphannattho (sī. pī.), nipphannatthova (syā.)] yathāsukhaṃ bhaṇeyya.
nipphādā.translation_1: A wise person should endure until it is accomplished; once accomplished, they may speak as they please.

kāvindo.meaning_2: lord of desires; master of pleasure; (name of) Kāma
kāvindo.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Found in the verse as kāvindo; the variant kāmindo is given in the edition. The form is probably a metathesis or scribal error for kāminda (kāma + inda); the PEU entry is uncertain. Nominative singular in the text, used as an epithet of Kāma.
kāvindo.example_1: 329. Ābādhoyaṃ asabbhirūpo, kāmindo [kāvindo (sī. pī.)] naradevena phuṭṭho;
kāvindo.translation_1: This affliction is unworthy of a noble person, the Lord of Desires (Kāma) touched by the king of men;

saṃhīro.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Vocative singular in the verse. Probably from saṃ + √har (carry away), i.e. 'carried away by' (cāmisena). PEU gives 'deceitful; easily deceived'.
saṃhīro.example_2: Yo cāmisena saṃhīro, hadayattheno ca yo naro.
saṃhīro.translation_2: Or to one who is swayed by material gain, or to a person who is a thief of hearts.

sambodhayati.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Third person singular present of the causative of sambujjhati, used here in the sense 'makes known, reveals'. The root is √budh (know, wake up).
sambodhayati.translation_2: The person who reveals a secret matter that was not understood;

tāvanto.meaning_2: so many; of that extent; as many
tāvanto.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Nominative singular masculine in the text, agreeing with ubbegā. Same formation as yāvant and etāvant.

paccanubhutva.meaning_2: having fully experienced; having enjoyed; having partaken of
paccanubhutva.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Alternative form paccanubhuyya (absolutive in -ya) is given in the text and is more common. The absolutive of paccanubhoti; variant spelling paccanubhotvā. Used with gandhe rase: having fully experienced smells and tastes.
paccanubhutva.example_1: Gandhe rase paccanubhuyya [paccanubhotva (syā.), paccanubhutva (pī.)] sabbaṃ, araññaṃ sādhu muni so pasattho.
paccanubhutva.translation_1: Having fully experienced all smells and tastes, the forest is good, the sage is praised.”

yime.meaning_2: these (parents) of yours; these for you
yime.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of tava (your) + ime (these). The text reads tavīme; the variant tava yime confirms the split. Nominative plural masculine.
yime.example_1: Jiṇṇā ca mātāpitaro tavīme [taveme (sī.), tava yime (syā. pī.)], passeyyuṃ taṃ vassasataṃ arogaṃ [arogyaṃ (syā. ka.)].
yime.translation_1: And these parents of yours are old; may they see you for a hundred years, free from disease.”

mokkhito.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Past participle used as a predicate in the verse; nominative singular referring to the speaker. The form is from the causative stem mokkha- (cf. moceti, mokkhati).
mokkhito.example_1: svāyaṃ gahīto na hi mokkhito me;
mokkhito.example_2: 346. Ayaṃ pure luddamakāsi kammaṃ, svāyaṃ gahīto na hi mokkhito me;
mokkhito.translation_2: “In the past I performed a cruel action, this result of that has been seized by me, and I am not released;

orundhiyā.meaning_2: having obstructed; having restrained; having blocked
orundhiyā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Absolutive in -iya (cf. orundhitvā) from ava + √rudh, with the initial o- by the usual ava > o contraction. Used adverbially before parirakkhissāmi; the PEU suggests the meaning 'having restrained/enclosed'.
orundhiyā.example_2: Orundhiyā naṃ parirakkhissāmi, māyaṃ puna luddamakāsi kammaṃ.
orundhiyā.translation_2: Restraining this, I will protect myself, so that I do not perform such cruel action again.”

ketakapupphanettaṃ.meaning_2: with eyes like ketaka flowers; whose eyes resemble screw-pine blossoms
ketakapupphanettaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Bahubbīhi compound describing a maiden's eyes. Accusative singular in the verse; fem form ketakapupphanettā would agree with kumāriṃ.
ketakapupphanettaṃ.example_2: 349. Passāmi vohaṃ daharaṃ [daharī (syā. pī. ka.)] kumāriṃ, mattūpamaṃ ketakapupphanettaṃ;
ketakapupphanettaṃ.translation_2: “I see a young maiden, like one intoxicated, with eyes like the ketaka flower;

abhutva.meaning_2: not having enjoyed; without having partaken (of)
abhutva.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Written abhutva in the text, variant of abhutvā; metrically shortened. In the Jātaka verse it is construed with bhoge, 'without having enjoyed the coils'.
abhutva.example_1: Abhuttabhoge [abhutva bhoge (syā. ka. aṭṭha.), abhutva bhoge (pī.), bhoge atutvā (ka.)] paṭhame vayasmiṃ, ādāya maccu vajate kumāriṃ.
abhutva.translation_1: In the prime of youth, without having enjoyed its coils, Death carries away the maiden.”

atutvā.meaning_2: having not enjoyed; without having experienced
atutvā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] A variant reading (ka.) for abhuttabhoge / abhutva bhoge in the first line; the sense is 'not having enjoyed'. Probably a miswriting of abhutvā. Absolutive, so stem and pattern are left empty.
atutvā.example_1: Abhuttabhoge [abhutva bhoge (syā. ka. aṭṭha.), abhutva bhoge (pī.), bhoge atutvā (ka.)] paṭhame vayasmiṃ, ādāya maccu vajate kumāriṃ.
atutvā.translation_1: In the prime of youth, without having enjoyed its coils, Death carries away the maiden.”

māgatā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi resolution of hatthattam āgatā; nominative plural of a past participle in -a agreeing with te.
māgatā.example_1: Ye ca bhutvāna vamiṃsu, te me hatthatta [hatthattha (sī. syā. pī.)] māgatā.
māgatā.translation_1: And those who, having eaten, vomited, they have come to my hand.”
māgatā.example_2: 42. ‘‘ Kathaṃ panime vihaṅgā [vihagā (sī. pī.)], tava hatthattamāgatā [hatthattha ’ māgatā (sī. syā. pī.)];
māgatā.translation_2: 42. “How did these birds come into your hands;

ekaceyyā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Metrical sandhi of ekacce (nom. pl. of ekacca, 'some') with iyyā; the sī. and pī. editions read ekacceyyā. The commentary may analyse it as ekacce + eyyā, but ekacce iyyā fits the sense. Variant reading in the verse.
ekaceyyā.example_1: 366. Hatthīhi assehi rathehi pattibhi, parivāritā muccare ekacceyyā [ekaceyyā (sī. pī.)];
ekaceyyā.translation_1: 366. Surrounded by horses, elephants, chariots, and infantry, some may be freed;

pitaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Alternate form of pitvā. The word in the text is a variant reading (syā.) where other editions have pitaṃ (hi taṃ). If read as pitaṃ, it would be pita (nt) meaning 'boiled/drink' or past participle of pivati. Here glossed as absolutive of pivati, 'having drunk', though the context is unclear.
pitaṃ.example_1: 370. Sarāni khīyanti saselakānanā, sabbaṃ hidaṃ [hi taṃ (sī. pī.), pitaṃ (syā.)] khīyati dīghamantaraṃ;
pitaṃ.translation_1: 370. Great lakes with their rocks and woods decay; all this decays over a long period;
pitaṃ.example_2: Sabbaṃ hidaṃ [hi taṃ (sī. pī.), pitaṃ (syā.)] bhañjare kālapariyāyaṃ, taṃ me matī hoti carāmi dhammaṃ.
pitaṃ.translation_2: All this is broken down by the passage of time; this I know, so I will practise the Dhamma.

nijjhapanaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text it is nominative/accusative singular, object of karonti: 'they make appeasement of them'. From nijjhapeti, causative of nijjhāyati, though the derivation is uncertain.

heṭṭhakā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the verse heṭṭhakā is nominative plural, listed with aparādhakā and dūsakā as people who wrong others; the sense is probably "low, base, despicable" rather than literally "lower". Could also be read as a variant of heṭṭhā.
heṭṭhakā.example_1: 377. Aparādhakā dūsakā heṭṭhakā ca, labhanti te rājino nijjhapetuṃ;
heṭṭhakā.translation_1: 377. Those who commit crimes, do wrong, or cause harm, can appease kings;

bhallātiya.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Proper name in a list of kings; no sandhi.
bhallātiya.example_2: Mātaṅga sambhūta sivi sirimanto, rohaṇa haṃsa sattigumbo bhallātiya;

supariṇāmavā.meaning_2: well rounded; fully developed; well matured
supariṇāmavā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading supariṇāmavā for supariṇāhavā ('well rounded'). Possessive suffix -vant with -nt dropped before the nominative ending. Describes a pitcher in the simile.
supariṇāmavā.translation_1: 2. Like a great water-bearing pitcher, fully rounded,

ruppapaṭṭaplamaṭṭhīva.grammar: sandhi, adj + adj + adj + adj + ind
ruppapaṭṭaplamaṭṭhīva.meaning_2: like one smeared with a silver plate; as if touched with a silver plaque
ruppapaṭṭaplamaṭṭhīva.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of ruppapaṭṭaplamaṭṭhī (adj) + iva; in the text it describes a tigress (byagghī iva). The spelling ruppapaṭṭapalimaṭṭhīva (syā.) and rūpapaṭṭapamaṭṭhīva (ka.) are variants; ruppa = silver. The word is an adjective describing one polished or smeared (palimaṭṭha) with silver plates.
ruppapaṭṭaplamaṭṭhīva.translation_1: 9. Like one polished with a silver plate, like a tigress born on the mountain slope,

rūpapaṭṭapamaṭṭhīva.meaning_2: as if pressed with a beautiful plate; as if burnished with a lovely slab
rūpapaṭṭapamaṭṭhīva.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading ruppapaṭṭapalimaṭṭhīva is preferred by the editors; doubt whether the first member is rūpa (beautiful) or ruppa (silver). -iva is sandhi of iva.
rūpapaṭṭapamaṭṭhīva.translation_1: 9. Like one polished with a silver plate, like a tigress born on the mountain slope,

ambuni.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Locative singular in the text (ambuni = ambu + ni). Related adjectives ambuda and ambuja suggest ambu means water.
ambuni.example_2: 15. Yaṃ kiñci ubhato tīre, phalaṃ patati ambuni;
ambuni.translation_2: 15. Whatever fruit falls into the water on either bank,

mabhisaṅgaṃ.meaning_2: do not indulge in attachment; do not delight in clinging
mabhisaṅgaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of mā + abhisaṅga (masc, 'attachment; clinging'). The word is mā + abhisaṅgaṃ in the text. The comment in the second sentence may translate abhisaṅga differently.
mabhisaṅgaṃ.translation_2: Do not indulge in longing, restrain yourself, lord of generations.

āceyyamāno.meaning_2: being desired; being sought after; being wished for
āceyyamāno.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Rare causative passive present participle from √ci 1 (gather; note, observe) with the -eyya- sign; the reading and analysis are uncertain. Vocative usage in the text, modifying rājisi.
āceyyamāno.translation_2: Royal sage, you who desire death while being one who should be honored.

cīyatī.meaning_2: is accumulated; accumulates; is heaped up
cīyatī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Passive of cināti; the text has cīyatī before tassa, a sandhi form of cīyati. Also explained in PEU as 'increases'.
cīyatī.example_2: Na cīyatī tassa narassa pāpaṃ, sace na ceteti vadhāya tassa.
cīyatī.translation_2: Bad kamma is not accumulated for that person, if he does not intend harm for that.

isipūgasamaññāte.meaning_2: known as the company of sages; designated as the assembly of hermits
isipūgasamaññāte.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Compound of isi + pūga + samaññāta (pp of samaññāti). Locative singular in the verse.
isipūgasamaññāte.example_2: 20. Isipūgasamaññāte, evaṃ lokyā viditā sati [pati (ka. syā. ka.)];
isipūgasamaññāte.translation_2: 20. Known among the assembly of sages, thus mindfulness is known in the world;

upānayāmi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] First person singular upānayāmi in the text; the related PEU entry gives upānayati as the 3rd singular.
upānayāmi.translation_2: I will lead you to a cool place, abide there without care.

pabodhare.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] 3rd plural present of the causative pabodheti (pa + budh + *e), with the ending -are for -enti. The text's pabodhare is a metrical or script variant; the sense is 'cuckoos awaken (the grove)'.
pabodhare.translation_2: Resound with flocks of swans, and cuckoos awaken [the grove] here.

kosumbhasalalā.meaning_2: kosiya flower; sesamum flower; name of a flowering tree or creeper used in garlands
kosumbhasalalā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Probably a dvanda compound of kosumba and salalā rather than a feminine a-stem headword. The text is a list of plants, with nīpa and the ripe tāla palms; kosumba is the kosiya or sesamum flower, salalā is uncertain. Spelling saḷalā in the Burmese and Siamese editions.
kosumbhasalalā.translation_1: Kosamba, śalala, nīpa, and ripe palms hang down.

tiriṭī.meaning_2: wearing a wreath (of flowers); adorned with a garland
tiriṭī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Descriptive compound in a list of ornaments; nominative singular in the verse. PEU gives tiriṭa as a small tree and tiriṭi as cicada, but the context suggests a floral ornament.
tiriṭī.translation_2: 28. Wearing garlands, wreaths, armlets, adorned with sandalwood,

aṅgadī.meaning_2: wearing an armlet; adorned with an armlet
aṅgadī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Bahubbīhi compound describing a person wearing aṅgadas. In these verses it is nominative singular, parallel with mālī, tiriṭī and kāyūrī.
aṅgadī.translation_2: 28. Wearing garlands, wreaths, armlets, adorned with sandalwood,

candanassado.meaning_2: scented with sandalwood; having the fragrance of sandalwood
candanassado.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading candanussada is given in the text. Nominative singular qualifying a king; a bahubbīhi compound describing the fragrance of sandalwood on the body.
candanassado.translation_1: 28. Wearing garlands, wreaths, armlets, adorned with sandalwood,

tiṭṭhasī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] 2nd person singular of tiṭṭhati; here paired with gacchasi, 'you go and stand'.
tiṭṭhasī.example_2: 34. So chinnavātaṃ kamasī aghamhi, vehāyasaṃ gacchasi tiṭṭhasī ca;
tiṭṭhasī.translation_2: Thou movest through the air, thou walkest there, and standest too.

dārukaṭallakova.meaning_2: wooden puppet; wooden figure; mechanical figure
dārukaṭallakova.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text it is dārukaṭallakova, i.e. dārukaṭallako + iva (like, as), in the nominative singular, used in a simile: 'so naccatī dārukaṭallakova' = 'he dances like a wooden puppet'.
dārukaṭallakova.example_2: So naccatī dārukaṭallakova, tassā puṇṇaṃ kumbhamimaṃ kiṇātha.
dārukaṭallakova.translation_2: One dances like a wooden puppet; buy this jar filled with that!

kalahāni.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Plural form in the verse (kalahāni). Alternatively could be read as adjective kalahin (quarrelsome), but the PEU and commentary support the neuter plural noun kalahāni. The root √kal 1 (spend time, disturb) is uncertain; some derive from √kalah (argue).
kalahāni.example_2: 44. Mānātimānā kalahāni pesuṇī, dubbaṇṇinī naggayinī palāyinī;
kalahāni.translation_2: It brings pride, arrogance, quarrels, and calumny; it is ugly, naked, and makes one flee.

pesuṇī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Feminine form used of a bad quality or of one who slanders; in the verse it describes a state (pride, arrogance, quarrels, slander). Could also be treated as a feminine noun "slander".
pesuṇī.example_2: 44. Mānātimānā kalahāni pesuṇī, dubbaṇṇinī naggayinī palāyinī;
pesuṇī.translation_2: It brings pride, arrogance, quarrels, and calumny; it is ugly, naked, and makes one flee.

dubbaṇṇinī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Feminine form of dubbaṇṇin used in this verse of the Mānatthaddha-jātaka; nominative singular in the text.
dubbaṇṇinī.example_2: 44. Mānātimānā kalahāni pesuṇī, dubbaṇṇinī naggayinī palāyinī;
dubbaṇṇinī.translation_2: It brings pride, arrogance, quarrels, and calumny; it is ugly, naked, and makes one flee.

naggayinī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] A descriptive feminine adjective used in a list of negative epithets, possibly personifying a woman lacking clothes or shamelessness.  Nom. sg. of an ī-stem; nominative singular in the text.
naggayinī.example_2: 44. Mānātimānā kalahāni pesuṇī, dubbaṇṇinī naggayinī palāyinī;
naggayinī.translation_2: It brings pride, arrogance, quarrels, and calumny; it is ugly, naked, and makes one flee.

niketo.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text niketо is nominative singular, co-ordinating with gatī in the phrase gatī niketo. Sometimes written niketо.
niketo.example_2: Corāna dhuttāna gatī niketo, tassā puṇṇaṃ kumbhamimaṃ kiṇātha.
niketo.translation_2: It is the path and home of thieves and scoundrels; buy this jar filled with that!

ucchedanī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Occurs in a Jātaka verse as a feminine adjective agreeing with an implied noun, describing a thing that ruins wealthy families. Scribe variants ucchedanī and ucchedanivitta are recorded for the second line.
ucchedanī.example_2: Ucchedanī vittavataṃ [ucchedanī vittagataṃ (syā.), ucchedanivittagataṃ (ka.)] kulānaṃ, tassā puṇṇaṃ kumbhamimaṃ kiṇātha.
ucchedanī.translation_2: this is the destruction of wealthy families; buy this jar filled with that!

ucchedanivittagataṃ.meaning_2: gone to the destruction of wealth; come to ruin of riches
ucchedanivittagataṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading of ucchedanī vittagataṃ; accusative singular agreeing with kumbhaṃ. The second element may also be analysed as vitta + gata, 'gone to (one's) wealth'.
ucchedanivittagataṃ.example_1: Ucchedanī vittavataṃ [ucchedanī vittagataṃ (syā.), ucchedanivittagataṃ (ka.)] kulānaṃ, tassā puṇṇaṃ kumbhamimaṃ kiṇātha.
ucchedanivittagataṃ.translation_1: this is the destruction of wealthy families; buy this jar filled with that!

nārādhayī.meaning_2: did not please; did not win over
nārādhayī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of na + ārādhayī (aorist 3rd singular of ārādhayati). Used in Jātaka verses.
nārādhayī.example_2: 73. Kiṃ kamma kubbaṃ tava deva pāva [devapāde (sī. syā. pī.)], nārādhayī taṃ tadicchāmi sotuṃ;
nārādhayī.translation_2: “What act or word of mine, lord, caused you to be displeased, that I wish to hear?

udassaye.meaning_2: places on; sets up; establishes; installs
udassaye.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] 3rd singular present causative, used in the sense 'you place (me) on the throne'. PEU suggests a possible alternative analysis as ud + √sī + si, but the causative of √as fits the sense better.
udassaye.example_2: Yamajja rajjamhi udassaye tuvaṃ, rajjampi niccheyyaṃ tayā vināhaṃ.
udassaye.translation_2: For today you wish to set me on the throne, yet I do not desire the kingdom without you.”

tuviyaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Possessive adjective from tumha; the form is accusative singular dependent on sarāmi. The PEU suggests tuviya, but that entry appears to describe the bare stem, while the text form is tuviyaṃ.
tuviyaṃ.example_2: 74. Na kammunā vā vacasā va tāta, aparādhitohaṃ tuviyaṃ sarāmi;
tuviyaṃ.translation_2: “Dear son, I do not recall a single unkind act or word of yours.

bhidā.meaning_2: breaking; splitting; piercing; (the act of) breaking
bhidā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Appears in the phrase bhidā rukkhasūle, possibly 'breaking (you) on a wooden stake'; the meaning is uncertain and the word may belong to a different noun or verb form. In the second sentence abhidā is probably a sandhi of abhidā or abhi + bhidā, not this word alone.
bhidā.example_2: Makarehi abhidā [makarehibbhidā (sī.), makarehi ’ bhidā (syā.), makarehi bhinnā (pī.)] nāvā, phalakenāhamaplaviṃ.
bhidā.translation_2: The ship was broken by sea monsters, and I drifted on a plank.

mājānamidhāvajeyya.meaning_2: may one not run here on account of (that) knowledge
mājānamidhāvajeyya.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi resolution uncertain; possibly mā + ājānaṃ + idha + āvajeyya (āvajeti = to turn towards, run). Text and context unavailable.

gamyā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Alternative reading for gantvā in the verse (Sinhalese and Thai editions read gamyā); the sense is 'having gone (to)'. Perhaps a misreading of a participle gata.
gamyā.example_1: Mātu ca [mātucca (sī.)] hetu paraloka gantvā [gamyā (sī. syā.), gamya (pī.)], sukhena saggena ca sampayutto.
gamyā.translation_1: And for the sake of my mother, having gone to the other world, I am conjoined with the happiness of being reborn in heaven.”

gamya.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading in the text for gamyā, a past participle used absolutely (paraloka gantvā/gamyā); the meaning is 'having gone to the other world'. The reading gamya may also be analysed as an absolutive with -ya.
gamya.example_1: Mātu ca [mātucca (sī.)] hetu paraloka gantvā [gamyā (sī. syā.), gamya (pī.)], sukhena saggena ca sampayutto.
gamya.translation_1: And for the sake of my mother, having gone to the other world, I am conjoined with the happiness of being reborn in heaven.”

saṅkhātajātīmaraṇohamasmi.grammar: sandhi, adj + nt + adj + pron + pr
saṅkhātajātīmaraṇohamasmi.meaning_2: I am one who has understood birth and death; I have comprehended birth and death
saṅkhātajātīmaraṇohamasmi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of saṅkhāta, jāti, maraṇa, ahaṃ and asmi; verse, first person singular. Possibly also analysed as a compound saṅkhātajātīmaraṇa + ahaṃ + asmi.
saṅkhātajātīmaraṇohamasmi.example_2: Saṅkhātajātīmaraṇohamasmi, yatheva me idha tathā parattha.
saṅkhātajātīmaraṇohamasmi.translation_2: I have understood birth and death; as it is for me here, so it is in the next world.”

sandīpayitvā.meaning_2: having kindled; having lit; having made bright; having shown clearly
sandīpayitvā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Absolutive of the causative sandīpeti (saṃ + √dīp, *e). The text's sandīpayitvā shows the causative vowel -aya- before -tvā. The gloss 'having kindled' fits the fire in the second sentence; 'having shown clearly' also fits the PEU. If a text variant sandīpetvā exists, it is the same word.
sandīpayitvā.example_2: Sandīpayitvā paṭivedayittha, ādīpito dāni mahāyamaggi [mayā yakkhamaggi (ka.)].
sandīpayitvā.translation_2: Having kindled it, he announced, ‘The great fire is now lit.’

kampilla.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading of kapila, a city name, in these Jātaka verses; the text has kampilla with kapila as the variant. Appears in the locative and with the accusative ending -am contraction in the second line. Possible sandhi with the following word.
kampilla.example_1: Evaṃ tuvaṃ porisādā pamutto, viroca kapile [kampilla (sī. pī.), kapille (syā.)] mahānubhāva;
kampilla.translation_1: So you, released from the ogre, shine in Kampilla, great one;
kampilla.example_2: Anuññāto sotthi sukhī arogo, paccāgamā [paccāga (pī.)] kapilamalīnasattā [kampilla ’ malīnasatto (sī. pī.), kapila ’ malīnasattā (ka.)].
kampilla.translation_2: Given permission, in safety, happy and healthy, returned to Kampilla.”

kampillamalīnasatto.meaning_2: whose mind is stained by (thoughts of) the kampilla tree; with heart defiled by kampilla
kampillamalīnasatto.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Compound of kampilla (a tree, possibly Premna serratifolia), malīna (stained, tainted) and satta (being; mind). Nominative singular in the text; exact sense uncertain.

jayadisajātakaṃ.meaning_2: Jayaddisa Jātaka; the birth story of King Jayaddisa
jayadisajātakaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Title of the third Jātaka in the Book of the Nines. The text reads jayadisa° (with one d, a variant); accusative singular in the sentence, as a title citation.

paṇḍūsi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text it is a vocative used in address to a woman ('paṇḍūsi varavaṇṇini'). The analysis as a compound with si is uncertain; possibly a variant of paṇḍu or a sandhi form. The PEU entries paṇḍaka and paṇḍara are not direct matches.
paṇḍūsi.translation_2: “Why do you grieve, O slender one, so pale, O fair-complexioned one?

poraṃ.meaning_2: formerly; in the past; of old
poraṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] The text prints poraṃ but the variant reading is puraṃ; taken here as an adverb meaning 'formerly', qualifying nigrodharājaṃ. Could also be puraṃ (ind, prep) 'before; in front of'.
poraṃ.example_1: Atha dakkhasī meghasamānavaṇṇaṃ, nigrodharājaṃ atha sahassapādaṃ [poraṃ (ka.)].
poraṃ.translation_1: Then you will see a cloud-colored one, the king of banyans, with a thousand shoots.”

bhimūla.meaning_2: having a terrible root; with a dreadful base
bhimūla.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading for tumūla in the verse; a compound of bhima (terrible, from √bhī) and mūla (root), meaning 'of terrible root/foundation'. The related entry bhimma (terrible) supports this analysis.
bhimūla.example_1: 108. Tiṭṭhanti te tumūlaṃ [tumūla (syā.), bhimūla (pī. ka.)] passasantā, kuppanti vātassapi eritassa;
bhimūla.translation_1: “They stand there breathing heavily, and they get angry even at the wind if it is stirred;
